title: Molten Aluminum-Induced Corrosion and Wear-Resistance Properties of ZrB<sub>2</sub>-Based Cermets Improved by Sintering-Temperature Manipulation.

recollection.intervention: Manipulation of sintering temperature during fabrication
recollection.structure: Likely densified ZrB2 cermets with varying microstructures depending on sintering temperature
recollection.mechanism: Higher sintering temperatures may improve grain bonding and reduce porosity, enhancing corrosion and wear resistance against molten aluminum
recollection.results: Probably found optimal sintering temperature that maximizes corrosion and wear resistance, with quantitative improvements in mass loss or wear rate compared to lower temperatures. (This is a guess.)

score.note: The recollection only restates generic sintering-temperature manipulation and plausibly suggests densification, better grain bonding, and reduced porosity. It does not identify SPS temperatures, the 1500 °C optimum, binder pore-filling versus 1600 °C binder loss, or any numerical corrosion, wear, density, hardness, toughness, or friction results.
